\subsection{Headline: both settings at once}
\label{sec:res-p1}
\label{sec:res-p2}
\label{sec:res-residual}
\label{sec:res-d25}
\label{sec:res-d26}

Table~\ref{tab:headline} and Fig.~\ref{fig:overview} give the main result. On the stream, Residual TFT-EWC is equivalent to linear extrapolation (0.32/0.31 against 0.34~pp) and beats GB-LAST by 0.24--0.46~pp. On unseen conditions it beats extrapolation by 0.43--0.68~pp; GB-ALL is better there because it stores every condition. Pretraining on 36{,}711 first-life samples did not help (+0.22~pp, replicated), and the 21 Spark inputs made the model worse.

\subsection{Continual learning and per-condition error (S1, S6)}
\label{sec:res-p3}
\label{sec:res-interp}
\label{sec:res-repro}
\label{sec:res-d24}

Fig.~\ref{fig:dash-s6} opens the S6 results up by task and condition. Over $h{=}1$--6, EWC cuts forgetting further, from 0.28/0.22 to 0.09~pp (replicated); shift-adaptive EWC and literature backbones (BiLSTM, TCN, Transformer, GPR) did not beat the residual TFT (supplement). Fig.~\ref{fig:dash-horizon} shows the gain over persistence growing with the horizon. On S1 all methods are level (0.46--0.48~pp) and every sample stays in class C0. An ablation credits the TFT's gain (0.89 to 0.40~pp) to dropping the diagnostics and adding the time between checks, not to the architecture.

\subsection{Reuse classes and intervals}
\label{sec:res-intervals}

The proposed model puts 95.5\% of held-out S6 samples in their measured reuse class (extrapolation 93.9\%, GB-ALL 97.7\%), and every error is off by one class only (classification metrics: supplement Table~SXV). Interval coverage holds only when calibrated on held-out conditions and fails out of range (Fig.~\ref{fig:dash-unseen}a).

\subsection{Many unseen conditions (S7, S10)}
\label{sec:res-many}

Under the no-storage rule the proposed model beats GB-LAST on S10 for both horizon sets ($p_{\mathrm{Holm}}<10^{-10}$) and on S7 for $h{=}1$--3 (Fig.~\ref{fig:dash-unseen}b--d; table: supplement Table~SXIV). GB-ALL, which stores every condition, stays better on 52 of 64 S10 and 50 of 60 S7 conditions; its higher S10 mean comes from a few calendar conditions where it fails (up to 17~pp).

\subsection{Bounded memory: the replay ensemble V2}
\label{sec:res-d38}

Keeping 40 rows per condition (post hoc; Fig.~\ref{fig:dash-d38}), V2 shows no replicated difference from the joint TFT and reaches pooled 90\% coverage of 0.89--0.91. It beats extrapolation and the earlier model on S7 and S10 and gradient boosting on S10, but there mostly where boosting fails (median gains 0.02--0.19~pp); coverage drops to 0.81--0.84 on S10 calendar and S7 cyclic conditions.
